hypotheses.justification: Choose ε using ReferencePath.exists_small_length hδ, so 0 < ε < δ and 2 * ε < rampLimit. Run the displayed compactness argument at ε, obtaining τ₀, α, M. From the definitions of continuation and primitive, slopeCutoff_one and intervalIntegral.integral_congr show that continuation δ G and continuation ε G agree on the open set {p | p.1 < ε}: both cutoffs equal 1 throughout the integration interval. Their Fréchet derivatives therefore agree there by Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq. Consequently referenceP1 and referenceP2 for widths δ and ε agree there. Taking τ = τ₀ / 2 transfers every bound to width δ and gives 0 < τ ≤ δ. This works for every retained δ > 0, however large; shrinking τ avoids any cutoff-boundary issue.
